title_from_archive: High-Resolution and High-Speed Laser Scanning Confocal Microscope; Deadline: 04-01-2026
notice_text: UNIVERSITYOFHYDERABAD (ACentralUniversityestablishedbyanActofParliament,1974) Prof. C. R. Rao Road, P.O. Central University Campus, Gachibowli, Hyderabad - 500 046, Telangana, INDIA website: www.uohyd.ac.in School of Life Sciences Department/of: Animal Biology Telephone:9110384948 Email:prasadtammineni@uohyd.ac.in Notice Inviting Tender No. UH/SLS/AB/PT/IA/Fluorescence microscopy /2025-26/01 date:13/11/2025 Sealed tenders are invited for supply of the following items under two bid systems from the reputed manufacturers or their authorized dealers to the University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad. Sealed bids should reach the office of the Dr. Prasad Tammineni, Room no. F-8, Department of Animal Biology, School of Life Sciences, University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad on or before 12/12/2025(date) 5.00 pm (time). Technical Specifications for High-Resolution and High-Speed Laser Scanning Confocal Microscope A Inverted Fluorescent Laser Scanning confocal Microscope with Live Cell Capability, with at least three laser lines, along with a super-resolution module for high-resolution imaging applications Bids are invited for a state-of-the-art imaging platform consisting confocal “Inverted fluorescent microscope with live cell imaging system, with at least three laser lines and a high-resolution module for a wide range of applications in life sciences and interdisciplinary sciences. OEM/authorized representatives can bid for any one/single part of the imaging platform. However, preference will be given to OEMs/their authorized representatives that can offer an integrated, robust imaging platform that can be upgradable to applications like, spinning disk, FRET, FRAP, FLIM and 2-camera system etc,. to fit into evolving research questions in the future. Sealed bids should reach the Tammineni lab, Room F8, School of Life Sciences, University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad on or before 04th Dec 2025 (Date) 5:30pm (time). Part A: A confocal ‘Inverted Fluorescent Microscope with Live Cell Capability Sl No Part A: Specification 1 Microscope: Fully Motorized Inverted Fluorescence Microscope for BF/Fluorescence with a dedicated remote touch panel/tab/controller and remote focus knob for controlling motorized components of the microscope. The system should be equipped with a built in Infinity port/stratum structure or double deck system for future laser introduction or FRAP upgradation/optical tweezer upgradation etc. The system should have proper drainage system to avoid any leakage from the dish into the precious optics. 2 Widefield tilting Binocular observation head with paired 10X eye pieces with dioptre adjustment. Bright LED light source for BF, DIC imaging applications controlled by imaging software and touch screen panel. 3 Programmable motorized X-Y scanning stage including sample holders for slides, 35/60 mm Petri dish, Labtech chambers and multi well dishes with multipoint, tile and mosaic imaging software (capable of fast 6D imaging). 4 Hardware & IR laser/LED (> 790 nm) Based Focus Drift compensation for long term live cell imaging application is mandatory and must be capable of working with plastic and cover glass bottom dishes. The drift compensator should be controlled by the remote touch screen panel with one touch autofocus to instantly focus the specimen mounted on plastic and glass bottom dishes. 5 Bright long working life LED Light Source with direct coupling for Fluorescence imaging, catering to the DAPI, CFP, YFP, FITC/GFP, RFP, mCherry, Cy3 and Cy5 fluorophores to be included. The light source should facilitate in capturing fast events with microsecond switching via TTL inputs via remote triggering (TTL, microsecond), Individual channel triggering (TTL, microsecond) for on/off control of selected channels. Triggering speed <20 μs at full power. A suitable TTL controller board/card should be supplied controlled by imaging software for fast switching of LED lines. 6 Narrow Band pass fluorescent filters cubes should include for DAPI, FITC/GFP, RFP/ mCherry Cy3 and Cy5 observation and imaging. 7 Motorized 6-position nosepiece with slots for DIC, Motorized Condenser with NA 0.55 or better with optical modules for DIC for respective objectives with built in transmitted shutter. 8 Minimum 8 position or higher motorized filter cube turret with built in motorized shutter for accommodating minimum 7 position fluorescent filters for sample visualization and camera-based imaging and one for BF/DIC Imaging 9 High precision Z-focus drive with step size of 10 nm or better. 10 Objectives: Plan super apochromat objectives - 40x/1.4 or better oil, 60/63x/1.42 oil immersion or better, 100X/1.45 oil or better, and confocal compatible lenses for 10X/0.40, Long Distance 20X/0.40 (WD 7.8 mm or better). DIC attachment for 20X, 40X, 60X and 100X should be the part of standard supply. All will be considered) the objectives should be plan Apo chromatically corrected. notice_text: 1 29/10/2025 Ref. No.: UoH/SEST/KVRSE/ARDB/DIC Global tender enquiry for the supply of One 3D digital image correlation system. The School of Engineering Sciences & Technology (SEST), University of Hyderabad (UoH), invites tenders in a two-bid format from highly reputed and established firms and authorized dealers to supply one 3D digital image correlation system which can operate at high temperatures also in addition to room temperature. Final Terms and Conditions are as per UoH's latest purchase policy. The tenders must reach the below given address below on or before 5.00 PM on November 21, 2025. THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS MUST BE STRICTLY MET IF THE QUOTATION IS TO BE VALID 1. All quotations should be addressed to below mentioned details and envelopes should be superscribed with the following: "One 3D, digital image correlation system": Prof. Koteswararao V. Rajulapati, School of Engineering Sciences & Technology, West Campus, University of Hyderabad Central University P.O., Gachibowli, Hyderabad 500046, INDIA. 2. Quotations must reach before 5 PM on 21.11.2025. Quotations received after the due date and time will not be considered. The University of Hyderabad will not, in any way, be responsible for any postal or other delays. 3. The bids shall be submitted in a TWO-BID format in separate sealed covers. Item code, enquiry number & due date must be compulsorily mentioned on both envelopes contained within another main envelope duly sealed, which shall also have item code, enquiry number + due date superscribed. a) TECHNO-COMMERCIAL BID Please give detailed specifications, International standards (BIS INTERNATIONAL), catalogues, list of users & technical details, technical compliance sheet, etc., along with the operating parameters, pre-installation requirements, payment terms, warranty/guarantee period, delivery period, etc., very explicitly without any ambiguity. The quotation must clearly specify the make and model of the equipment. All relevant technical literature/brochures, application notes, and specifications must also be provided, adequately explaining and confirming compliance of the features of the model of the equipment being quoted with those given in the UoH tender enquiry. Without this, the quotation may be considered invalid. It must be clearly indicated if any of the features do not match. Explanations on the non-matching specifications will be considered. The UNIVERSITY OF HYDERABAD SCHOOL OF ENGINEERING SCIENCES & TECHNOLOGY CENTRAL UNIVERSITY P.O, PROF. C. R. RAO ROAD, GACHIBOWLI, HYDERABAD –500046, INDIA 2 University of Hyderabad reserves the right to determine which deviations are substantial based on current and future requirements. If features in the quoted equipment are better than those indicated in the enquiry, they must also be clearly explained. b) PRICE BID Giving full prices in foreign currency or in Indian rupees for Main equipment Essential accessories & spares. All optional items Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) charges for three years after the expiry of the warranty period. 4. Price & insurance: The price quoted should be as follows – In case of Indian suppliers : Insurance and freight prepaid by the vendor, Free delivery at the School of Engineering Sciences and Technology, University of Hyderabad. In case of foreign suppliers/import: CIP, HYDERABAD AIRPORT BASIS Note: The offers of the firms that quoted on Ex-works basis and do not mention the handling, documentation, packing, forwarding, transportation & insurance charges, etc., separately will not be considered as a responsive bid, and the acceptance of such bid will vest entirely with the University of Hyderabad. 5. Vendor qualification criteria for acceptance of technical bid. a) Vendor should have supplied at least 5 DIC Systems to Govt Organizations/Research Institutes in the past 5 years. Copy of Installation Report / Certificate must be submitted. b) Vendor must explicitly mention and provide proof of the items claimed under Make in India Scheme. c) Vendor must visit University of Hyderabad with their DIC System and demonstrate and validate the DIC measurements with available experimental data OR compare DIC Data with Strain Gage Extensometer and prove the accuracy of the DIC System. Vendor must also demonstrate High Temperature DIC upto 600 ºC. All travel costs to be borne by the vendor. ALL OPTIONS SHOULD BE QUOTED SEPARATELY. 6. Validity of prices: The quoted prices must be valid for a minimum period of 6 months from the date of opening of the bid, failing which offers may be summarily rejected by the University of Hyderabad. 7. Compliance statement: a. All manufacturers/agents must submit the compliance statement and the technical bid. b. Please provide the below details if you have supplied similar or identical items in India, particularly to other research/academic institutions in the last three years. ❖ Name of the item with brief specifications, model etc., ❖ Name & contact address of the user. ❖ Any other relevant information. 8. Installation & commissioning: Installation & commissioning will be the sole responsibility of the supplier / Indian agent. The supplier must do installation & commissioning with all infrastructural works. All vendors/agents must submit full details and requirements for installation & commissioning of the items as per the technical specifications they submitted. 9. Taxes, duties, and levies: The suppliers shall be solely responsible for all taxes, duties, levies, including Octroi, local levies, sales tax, and excise duties incurred as per extant laws in India. No concessional sales tax form "C" or 3 "D" will be issued by this University. It should be clearly mentioned in the quote whether the prices include taxes & duties. If the price includes taxes and a variation of tax element is sought, then the quote should mention the base level of taxes built into the price. 10. Customs and Excise Duty Exemption: The University of Hyderabad is under the University Grants Commission (UGC), Government of India, and thus is exempted from excise duty vide GOI notification No.10/97 central excise dated March 1, 1997, and is eligible for concessional customs duty as per GOI notification No.51/96 customs dated 23/07/1996 – amended from time to time. 11. Delivery Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) / BidSecurity: The bidders should furnish bid security for 5% of the estimated cost of the equipment along with their technical bid in the form of Account Payee Demand Draft / Banker’s Cheque from any of the Commercial Banks in an acceptable form, drawn in favour of Finance Officer, University of Hyderabad, payable at Hyderabad. If the bidder furnishes a Fixed Deposit Receipt / Bank Guarantee, the instrument shall be issued in favour of Finance Officer, University of Hyderabad, payable at Hyderabad and shall be valid for a period of 135 days from the date of opening technical bids. The MSE units registered with MSME and certificates obtained from NSIC under the Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS) shall be exempted from payment of Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) on production of requisite proof in respect of valid certification from NSIC. 12. Delivery locotion, Delivery Period, and Penalty Clauses: a) The items shall be delivered to: School of Engineering Sciences and Technology University of Hyderabad, Gachibowli, Hyderabad - 500 046, India. b) In case of foreign suppliers, the firm delivery period (in weeks) after opening an irrevocable Letter of Credit (L.C.) must be given in the Techno-commercial Bid. No part shipment is permitted. c) In the case of indigenous suppliers, the firm delivery period (in weeks) after the issue of the purchase order must be specified in the technical bid. Delivery is to be made at the University of Hyderabad. Delivery must be on a freight-paid basis for dispatch by road. University of Hyderabad will issue the certificate/declaration instead of a road permit to affect the delivery. d) In the event of delay in delivery beyond stipulated period indicated in the Purchase Order, liquidated damages @ 1% per each week of delay subject to a maximum of 5% of the cost of the order will be levied and collected by the University, by way of deduction from the payments due to the vendor/supplier. e) Delay in installation & commissioning beyond the contractual deadline will result in forfeiture of the performance bank guarantee. 13. Warranty: The supplier must warrant that the goods supplied under the contract are new, unused, and the most recent or current, and incorporate all recent improvements in design and materials as per specifications in this tender document. All vendors (manufacturers/agents) must submit offers with 36 months of comprehensive warranty after installation & successful commissioning of the equipment at the School of Engineering Sciences & Technology, University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad-500046, India, which would be considered for the tender evaluation purpose. The supplier should, however, quote separately for a comprehensive warranty for three successive years after completing a three-year comprehensive warranty. (This is to get an estimate of the cost involved). The warranty offered should be unconditional, and the seller should agree to replace or repair the equipment at his cost. The spare parts for the warranty repair have to be provided by the vendor. 14. Payment : a) For Indian suppliers and manufacturers - 100% payment subject to submission of 10 % 4 performance bank guarantee (PBG) as per clause four will be made direct to Indian suppliers by "Account Payee" cheque against invoice within 30 days of delivery, inspection, successful commissioning & acceptance of equipment/services by the University of Hyderabad. b) For Foreign suppliers, 100 % by irrevocable foreign letter of credit, subject to the vendor submitting an unconditional PBG from a scheduled bank of 10 % of FOB value, and before opening irrevocable L.C. This PBG must be valid for 60 days after the warranty period. c) Intermediary agencies, local representatives of foreign manufacturers/suppliers, are involved in importing foreign goods, and an authorization letter/certificate must be obtained to this extent. No agency commission shall be paid to such intermediary agencies/local representatives. d) In case of L.C.s, bank charges outside India, including confirmation charges, if any, shall be to the supplier's account. The documents for payment shall be presented to the purchaser's bank by the supplier within 21 days of shipment of the equipment. e) An agreement per standard University norms to be entered with the University before the opening of L.C. 15. Agreement: An Agreement in the format prescribed by the University of Hyderabad is required to be entered into by the Suppliers or their authorized Representative with the University in respect of purchase of one 3D, digital image correlation system. within a period of 15 days fromthe date of issue of Purchase Order. 16. Risk Purchase Clause: If the supplier fails to deliver the ordered one 3D, digital image correlation system within the stipulated delivery period specified in the Purchase Order, the University may resort to procure such items and in such a manner as deemed appropriate, goods or services similar to those undelivered, and the Supplier will be liable to reimburse the University for any excess costs for such similar goods or services. 17. Risk to reject: The University reserves the right to reject any or all the bids or accept a part of the quotation without assigning any reasons therefor. The decision of the University in this regard is final and binding on all the suppliers. 18. Resolution of disputes: Any disputes arising out of this contract shall be referred to the University, and if any of the parties here to is dissatisfied with the decision, the dispute shall be referred to the decision of the Arbitrator, who should be acceptable to both the parties, to be appointed by the Vice- Chancellor of the University. The decision of such Arbitrator shall be final and binding on both the parties 19. Jurisdication of courts: Disputes, if any, arising during course of execution of the order are to be settled within the jurisdiction of Hyderabad / Ranga Reddy District Courts only 20. Delay in submission: The University will not in any way be responsible for any postal / courier delay. Bids received beyond the stipulated date and time of submission are summarily rejected. Tenders incomplete in any respect will be summarily rejected. 21. Opening of tenders / bids: a) The bids will be opened at the School of Engineering Sciences and Technology, University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad in the presence of bidders or their authorised representatives. b) The authorised representative shall bring the authorisation letter and submit the same to the University before opening of bids. On failure to do so, the Representative loses the right to participate in the bid opening process. 5 22. This procurement is entirely governed by the University of Hyderabad Purchase Policy (UHPP). The University of Hyderabad reserves the right to reject any/all quotations or accept any offer or part thereof, without giving any reasons. Its decision in the matter will be final. 23. Any clarifications regarding this tender enquiry should be sought from the undersigned before submission of a formal quotation. Prof. Koteswararao V. Hence, all the contractors are requested to remind the following details. Submission of Quotations:- 23 .10.2025 upto 12.00 PM Opening of Quotations:- 23 .10.2025 at 3.00 PM S.No Name of the work Estimated Cost 1 Maintenance of Buildings: ” Clearing of chocked sewer lines at MH-I“ in UoH campus Rs. 49,750/- Sd/- Executive Engineer A/C 2 Name of work :- Maintenanace of Buildings- "Cleaning of Chocked Sewer lines at MH-I " in UoH Campus. 1) The estimate amount is inclusive of GST. 2) Comparative statement for Quoted rates shall be based on rates inclusive of GST. SCHEDULE OF QUANTITIES S. No D.S.R.No. Description of item Qty Unit Rate in figures & Rate in words Amount 1 14.77 Cleaning of chocked sewer line by diesel running vehicle mounting hydraulic operated high pressure suction cum jetting sewer cleaning machine fitted with pump having 4000 litres suction capacity and 6000 litres water jetting tank capacity including skilled operator, supervising engineer etc. for cleaning and partial desilting of manholes and dechocking of sewer lines. Dechocking and flushing of sewer line from one manhole to another by high pressure jetting system of 2200 PSI for sewer line from 150mm dia upto 300mm dia for all depth. 150.00 Rmt Rs Rupees Total Amount in figures Rs 3 Less Rebate Offered if any in words 1) The estimate amount is inclusive of GST. 2) Comparative statement for Quoted rates shall be based on rates inclusive of GST. Signature of the Contractor sd/- ExecutiveEngineer 4 Terms & Conditions: 1. The work should be completed within thirty (15) days from the date of issue of work order. Failure to complete the work within the stipulated time will entail recovery of compensation from work bills as decided by the University Engineer. 2. The contractor should abide by the Labour Laws, Minimum Wages Act & Workmen’s Compensation Act. 3. This work order can be cancelled and the work stopped at any time by the Officer-in-charge of the work or by any Officer superior to him in authority. 4. The contractor shall permit the University at the time of making intermediate payment(s) to deduct 10% of the value of the work billed for towards Security Deposit. The deposit is liable to be forfeited for non-rectification of defects pointed out to him during the execution of the work/Defect Liability Period. 5. The work shall be done as per CPWD specifications and as directed by the University Engineer from time to time. 6. If water is supplied by the University 1 % of the actual cost of water consuming items will be recovered from the bills for work done. 7. Seignorage charges will be deducted from the bill as per the stipulated rates communicated by the Govt. from time to time. 8. Defect liability period (6) months from the date of completion of the work. 9. For delay or slow progress of work the relevant clauses of CPWD manual will be invoked and penalty levied. 10. A.E (C- ) has to enclose the work completion certificate and user department certificate along with the bill. 11. No quotation will be accepted without PAN/GST no. 12. GST(2%)/TDS (1% or 2%) / Labour welfare cess (1%) will be levied wherever applicable. CC to: 1. Executive Engineer 1. A.E. Sub-Division (C- ) 2. S O (Works & Bills), 3. Finance & Account 4. O.C., 5. D.B., Sd/- Executive Engineer

title_from_archive: Maintenance of buildings: Providing external painting to Health Centre in UoH campus; Deadline: 04-08-2025
notice_text: UNIVERSITY OF HYDERABAD University Works Department Office of the Executive Engineer University of Hyderabad Central University P.O Hyderabad 500 046, Ph: 23132300 NOTE Ref: UH/ENGG/UE/2025-26/ Date: 30.07.2025 The Opening of Quotations (Below Rs. 50,000/-) for the above works mentioned below is scheduled to be held on 04.08.2025 at 12.00 PM in the Office of the University Works Department. Hence, all the contractors are requested to remind the following details. Submission of Quotations:- 04.08.2025 upto 12.00 PM Opening of Quotations:- 04.08.2025 at 3.00 PM S.No Name of the work Estimated Cost 1 Maintenance of buildings: Providing external painting to Health Centre in UoH campus Rs. 49,600/- Sd/- Executive Engineer A/C Name of work :- Maintenance of Buildings - "Providing External painting to Health Centre" in UoH Campus. 1) The Bidder should quote rates inclusive of GST. 2) All the below item rates are all inclusive of GST. SCHEDULE OF QUANTITIES S. No D.S.R.No. Description of item Qty Unit Rate in figures & Rate in words Amount 1 13.88 Removing white or colour wash by scrapping and sand papering and preparing the surface smooth including necessary repairs to scratches etc. complete 317.00 Sqm Figure: Rs____________________ Words: Rupees________________ ____________________________ 2 13.111 Finishing walls with Acrylic Smooth exterior paint of required shade : 317.00 Sqm Figure: Rs____________________ Words: Rupees________________ ____________________________ 13.111.1 Old work (Two or more coat applied @ 1.67 ltr/ 10 sqm) on existing cement paint surface). 3 13.99 Painting with synthetic enamel paint of approved brand and manufacture of required colour to give an even shade : 62.00 Sqm Figure: Rs____________________ Words: Rupees________________ ____________________________ 13.99.1 One or more coats on old work Total Amount in figures Rs Less Rebate Offered if any_______________________________________________________________________ Net Amount ___________________________________________________________________________________ Net Amount in words_____________________________________________________________________________ Sd/- Signature of the Contractor Executive Engineer Terms & Conditions: 1. The work should be completed within __________ from the date of issue of work order. Failure to complete the work within the stipulated time will entail recovery of compensation from work bills as decided by the University Engineer. 2. The contractor should abide by the Labour Laws, Minimum Wages Act & Workmen’s Compensation Act. 3. This work order can be cancelled and the work stopped at any time by the Officer-in-charge of the work or by any officer superior to him in authority. 4. The contractor shall permit the University at the time of making intermediate payment(s) to deduct 10% of the value of the work billed for towards Security Deposit. The deposit is liable to be forfeited for non- rectification of defects pointed out to him during the execution of the work/Defect Liability Period. 5. The work shall be done as per CPWD specifications and as directed by the University Engineer from time to time. 6. If water is supplied by the University 1% of the actual cost of water consuming items will be recovered from the bills for work done. 7. Seignorage charges will be deducted from the bill as per the stipulated rates communicated by the Govt. from time to time. 8. For delay or slow progress of work the relevant clauses of CPWD manual will be invoked and penalty levied. 9. Defect liability period Six (06) Months from the date of completion of the work. 10. TDS (1% or 2%) Labour welfare cess (1%) will be levied wherever applicable. 11. Value of work is inclusive of GST at applicable rate. 12. The GST invoice form should be filled and submitted along with the bill. Sd/- Executive Engineer CC to: 1. A.E. Sub-Division (Civil-I) 2. Office Copy

Sd/- Signature of the Contractor Executive Engineer 3 Terms & Conditions: 1. The work should be completed within Seven (07) days from the date of issue of work order. The contractor should abide by the Labor Laws, Minimum Wages Act & Workmen’s Compensation Act. 3. This work order can be cancelled and the work stopped at any time by the Officer-in-charge of the work or by any Officer superior to him in authority. 4. The contractor shall permit the University at the time of making intermediate payment(s) to deduct 10% of the value of the work billed for towards Security Deposit. The deposit is liable to be forfeited for non-rectification of defects pointed out to him during the execution of the work/Defect Liability Period. 5. The work shall be done as per CPWD specifications and as directed by the University Engineer from time to time. 6. If water is supplied by the University 1% of the actual cost of water consuming items will be recovered from the bills for work done. 7. Seignories charges will be deducted from the bill as per the stipulated rates communicated by the Govt. from time to time. 8. Defect liability period 6 (six) months from the date of completion of the work. 9. For delay or slow progress of work the relevant clauses of CPWD manual will be invoked and penalty levied. 10. A.E (C-) has to enclose the work completion certificate and user department certificate along with the bill. 11. No quotation will be accepted without PAN/VAT no. 12. TDS (1% or 2%) / Labor welfare cess (1%) will be levied wherever applicable. Sd/- Executive Engineer CC to: 1. Executive Engineer 2. A.E. Sub-Division (C-I) 3 File

Single tee with door. 110x110x110 mm. Make: Supreme/ Prince/ Finolex/ Astral. 4.00 Each Figure: Rs_________________ Words: Rupees_____________ __________________________ 11/b 12.42.5.2 Providing and fixing on wall face unplasticised - PVC moulded fittings/ accessories for unplasticised Rigid PVC rain water pipes conforming to IS : 13592 Type A, including jointing with seal ring conforming to IS : 5382, leaving 10 mm gap for thermal expansion. Bend 87.5°. 110 mm bend. Make: Supreme/ Prince/ Finolex/ Astral. 4.00 Each Figure: Rs_________________ Words: Rupees_____________ __________________________ 12 17.2.1 Providing and fixing white vitreous china pedestal type water closet (European type) with seat and lid, 10 litre low level white vitreous china flushing cistern & C.P. flush bend with fittings & C.I. brackets, 40 mm flush bend, overflow arrangement with specials of standard make and mosquito proof coupling of approved municipal design complete, including painting of fittings and brackets, cutting and making good the walls and floors wherever required : W.C. pan with ISI marked white solid plastic seat and lid. Sd/- Signature of the Contractor Executive Engineer A/c Terms & Conditions: 1. The work should be completed within __________ from the date of issue of work order. Failure to complete the work within the stipulated time will entail recovery of compensation from work bills as decided by the University Engineer. 2. The contractor should abide by the Labour Laws, Minimum Wages Act & Workmen’s Compensation Act. 3. This work order can be cancelled and the work stopped at any time by the Officer-in-charge of the work or by any officer superior to him in authority. 4. The contractor shall permit the University at the time of making intermediate payment(s) to deduct 10% of the value of the work billed for towards Security Deposit. The deposit is liable to be forfeited for non- rectification of defects pointed out to him during the execution of the work/Defect Liability Period. 5. The work shall be done as per CPWD specifications and as directed by the University Engineer from time to time. 6. If water is supplied by the University 1% of the actual cost of water consuming items will be recovered from the bills for work done. 7. Seignorage charges will be deducted from the bill as per the stipulated rates communicated by the Govt. From time to time. 8. For delay or slow progress of work the relevant clauses of CPWD manual will be invoked and penalty levied. 9. Defect liability period Six (06) Months from the date of completion of the work. 10. TDS (1% or 2%) Labour welfare cess (1%) will be levied wherever applicable. 11. Value of work is inclusive of GST at applicable rate. 12. The GST invoice form should be filled and submitted along with the bill. Sd/- Executive Engineer (A/C) CC to: 1. A.E. Sub-Division (Civil-II) 2. Office Copy

The bidder should also submit self-attested copies of relevant IT returns, PAN no, valid Registration Certificate and minimum 3-5 years Experience in similar projects shall sign all the schedule pages of bid without fail. 3. The bidders except Micro and Small Medium Enterprises (MSEs) notified under MSME, Procurement Policy (as per Rule 170 of GFR 2017), should pay EMD of 2% of Estimated Cost drawn in favor of “Finance Officer, University of Hyderabad” payable at Hyderabad. 4. Work to be carried out in the presence and under supervision of UWD Engineers. 7. The site shall be made available as and when required for execution of work. 8. Signature of the Contractor 3 15 Defect liability period of 6 Month commences from the date of satisfactory completion of work. 16 For delay or slow progress of work, relevant clauses of CPWD manual will be invoked and penalty levied. Signature of the Contractor 4 NAME OF WORK :- Ground water study in University of Hyderabad campus 1) The estimates amount is inclusive of GST. 2) The bidder should quote basic rates exclusive of GST and quote GST percentage separately; GST should be revised from time to time. S.No Description of items Qty Unit Basic Rate in Figures to be entered by the Bidder without GST Add: GST (%) Total Amount without GST Total Amount with GST 1 Conduct a comprehensive Hydrological study of the University campus to analyze 20 years of water consumption trends, assess underground aquifers and groundwater flow, evaluate current recharge mechanisms, delineate zonation based on yield, quality, recharge extent and geology, determine the linkage between surface and subsurface water systems, assess the impact of nearby construction on groundwater levels, and propose a detailed water conservation plan including recharge strategies, borewell locations, and projected groundwater yields 17.00 Cases Each Cases Sd/- Sd/- Sd/- Signature of the Contractor University Engineer Executive Engineer A/C D'M Gr-I 5

Technical Specifications for High-Resolution and High-Speed Spinning Disk Laser Scanning Confocal Microscope A spinning Disk Inverted Fluorescent Laser Scanning confocal Microscope with Live Cell Capability (Part A), with at least three laser lines (Part B), along with a super-resolution module (Part C) for high-resolution imaging applications Bids are invited for a state-of-the-art imaging platform consisting of three parts (part A: Spinning Disk confocal “Inverted fluorescent microscope with live cell imaging system, with at least three laser lines (part B), and a high-resolution module (Part C) for a wide range of applications in life sciences and interdisciplinary sciences. OEM/authorized representatives can bid for any one/single part of the imaging platform. However, preference will be given to OEMs/their authorized representatives that can offer solutions for all three parts to make an integrated, robust imaging platform. Sealed bids should reach the Tammineni lab, Room F8, School of Life Sciences, University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad on or before 28th May 2025 (date) 5:30pm (time). Part A: A Spinning Disk confocal ‘Inverted Fluorescent Microscope with Live Cell Capability Sl No Part A: Specification 1 Microscope: Fully Motorized Inverted Fluorescence Microscope for BF/Fluorescence with a dedicated remote touch panel/tab/controller and remote focus knob for controlling motorized components of the microscope. The system should be equipped with a built in Infinity port/stratum structure or double deck system for future laser introduction or FRAP upgradation/optical tweezer upgradation etc. The system should have proper drainage system to avoid any leakage from the dish into the precious optics. 2 Widefield tilting Binocular observation head with paired 10X eye pieces with dioptre adjustment. Bright LED light source for BF, DIC imaging applications controlled by imaging software and touch screen panel. 3 Programmable motorized X-Y scanning stage including sample holders for slides, 35/60 mm Petri dish, Labtech chambers and multi well dishes with multipoint, tile and mosaic imaging software (capable of fast 6D imaging). 4 Hardware & IR laser/LED (> 790 nm) Based Focus Drift compensation for long term live cell imaging application is mandatory and must be capable of working with plastic and cover glass bottom dishes. The drift compensator should be controlled by the remote touch screen panel with one touch autofocus to instantly focus the specimen mounted on plastic and glass bottom dishes. 5 Bright long working life LED Light Source with direct coupling for Fluorescence imaging, catering to the DAPI, CFP, YFP, FITC/GFP, RFP, mCherry, Cy3 and Cy5 fluorophores to be included. The light source should facilitate in capturing fast events with microsecond switching via TTL inputs via remote triggering (TTL, microsecond), Individual channel triggering (TTL, microsecond) for on/off control of selected channels. Triggering speed <20 μs at full power. A suitable TTL controller board/card should be supplied controlled by imaging software for fast switching of LED lines. 6 Narrow Band pass fluorescent filters cubes should include for DAPI, FITC/GFP, RFP/ mCherry Cy3 and Cy5 observation and imaging. 7 Motorized 6-position nosepiece with slots for DIC, Motorized Condenser with NA 0.55 or better with optical modules for DIC for respective objectives with built in transmitted shutter. 8 Minimum 8 position or higher motorized filter cube turret with built in motorized shutter for accommodating minimum 7 position fluorescent filters for sample visualization and camera-based imaging and one for BF/DIC Imaging 9 High precision Z-focus drive with step size of 10 nm or better. 10 Objectives: Plan super apochromat objectives - 40x/1.4 or better oil, 60/63x/1.42 oil immersion or better, 100X/1.45 oil or better, and confocal compatible lenses for 10X/0.40, Long Distance 20X/0.40 (WD 7.8 mm or better). DIC attachment for 20X, 40X, 60X and 100X should be the part of standard supply. All will be considered) the objectives should be plan Apo chromatically corrected. All the plan apochromatic objectives should have chromatic correction from 400-1000 nm both laterally and axially (<200nm axial between DAPI and Cy5) for precise colocalization studies in XYZ. (Please provide necessary data on website / brochure) The plan Apochromatic objectives should have uniform field of view (FOV) throughout wide FOV of large Chip SCMOS (>21mm). Low Fluorescence Immersion Oil 100ml should be provided (minimum 5 bottles). 11 Stage top CO2 incubator setup for long-term live cell imaging including incubation system with Temperature, CO2 and humidity control. The parameters for incubation system should be controlled by software with the ability to record the temperature, CO2 levels at peridics intervals of atleast 10 minutes . Temp collar/Objective heater for High NA objectives should be provided. 12 SPINNING DISK CONFOCAL: Fully automated and motorized Microlens based dual Nipkow disk scanning unit: The Scan Head should have at least 2/dual disks with micro lens on both excitation and emission disk (SoRa disc equivalent). The system should have 50 µm pinhole disk with microlenses on each pinhole of the disks & should have Super Resolution technology based on SoRa Disk (Super Resolution via Optical Re- Assignment) to enhance the excitation and resolution efficiency. The motorized spinning disk should have a minimum scan speed of 4000 rpm or more, automatically synchronized with camera speed. The system should have an appropriate optical module to make the FOV uniform, either on the excitation or emission side (a homogenizer/ uniformizer or equivalent is required). The system should be equipped with 1X intermediate magnification and a 3.2 times magnification motorized changer between the microscope and scan head completely controlled by the imaging software for switching between 1X and 3.2X. The scan head should have built in camera attachment port with three positions motorized excitation dichroic mirror slider with DMs for at least 405, 488, 561, 640 and a bye pass for BF DIC Imaging and built in 8-10 position emission filter wheels with narrow band emission filters for DAPI, FITC, TRITC, mCherry and Cy5. The system should deliver SoRa based super resolution imaging with XY resolution of 100-120nm and a speed of 100fps at full resolution in real time. The super resolution should be achieved with Optical Pixel reassignment for the spinning disk. The super resolution should be a proven technology with optical theory with published documents on the technology be provided. The super resolution processing software should be real time and be based on structured illumination with selective high frequency pattern collection of demodulated emission signal in real time and and not by mere 3D deconvolution. However, the lateral and axial resolution should further be enhanced by a dedicated on the fly/realtime 3D deconvolution algorithm fitting the PSF of above mentioned 120nm SR images. The system should be provided with dedicated on the fly 3D deconvolution software, fully integrated in the imaging software from the microscope manufacturer. The 3D deconvolution software should be real-time/instant/on the fly and should have dedicated algorithms for BF, widefield, point scanning LSM, Spinning disc LSM, Super Res and Multiphoton imaging. It should fetch meta data automatically from the images and should be able to generate and import realistic PSF data from bead samples. The software should be able to calibrate and perform 3D deconvolution of images from other microscope image formats as well. The saved native image format should be compatible with image J/Fiji to open and with meta data and calibration file. Part B Specifications: Lasers All lasers should be the latest solid-state lasers with following laser wavelengths and powers. a. 477/488 nm: 100 mW or better b. 555/561 nm, 100 mW or better c. 638/640 nm: 100 mW or better All the Lasers should be stable solid-state laser controlled by Direct Modulation/AOTF for precise switching and swift selection of the desired laser lines. The laser combiner should onsite be upgradable to additional lasers such as 405, 445, 514 and 594nm. All lasers should be combined with high transmission beam splitters and delivered to the confocal scan head through high transmission efficiency optical fiber. The laser control should be through direct Modulation by high speed break out box for ultra-fast ON/OFF control and intensity modulation with individual laser lines, continuously variable (0 % - 100 %, 1 % increments). Online/real-time deconvolution. The devise should support fast two color near simultaneous imaging using single camera with perfect over lapping of two colors. The process of closing the shutter and moving the filter wheels & Z steps should begin as soon as camera acquisition is done, during camera chip readout to avoid bleaching. notice_text: Page 1 UNIVERSITY OF HYDERABAD {Establishment by the act of the Parliament in 1974} Gachibowli, Hyderabad TENDER SCHEDULE FOR THE WORK OF MAINTENANCE OF BUILDINGS:-SUPPLY AND FILLING OF STONE, SAND AND MOORUM FOR HT STRUCTURE YARDS OF ALL SUBSTATIONS IN THE UNIVERSITY OF HYDERABAD CAMPUS. C O N T R A C T O R ESTIMATED COST Rs. 42,56,700/- (Inclusive of GST) EMD Rs. 85,134/- F & A Receipt No. _ _ Book No. _______ Time for the Completion of work: 2 Month FROM ___________TO _____________ WORK ORDER REFERANCE: EXPENDITURE CHARGABLE TO: Bid Submission start date (Online) : 01.03.2025 up to 3.00 P.M. Bid Submission close date (Online) : 12.03.2025 up to 3.00 P.M. Bid opening date (Online) : 13.03.2025 at 3.00 P.M (Technical Bid) Date of opening of financial bids of technically qualified bidders will be intimated through Central Public Procurement Portal. Sd/- Assistant Engineer (E) Sd/- UNIVERSITY ENGINEER Page 2 UNIVERSITY OF HYDERABAD {Establishment by the act of the Parliament in 1974} Gachibowli, Hyderabad. University Works Department, Ph no.040-23132306/040-23101208 E-mail: aet.uohyd@gmail.com E-TENDER FOR NOTICE INVITING TENDER (NIT) Notice Inviting e-Tender No. UH/ENGG/UWD/2024-25/61 Name of the work Maintenance of Buildings:-Supply and filling of Stone, Sand and Moorum for HT Structure yards of all Substations in the University of Hyderabad Campus. Estimated Cost Rs.42,56,700/- (Inclusive of GST) Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) Rs. 85,134/- (Through DD or Bank Guarantee) Performance Guarantee 5% of the Tendered value i.e 2,12,835/- Time Allowed 2 Month Date of Start of Bid Submission 01.03.2025 at 3.00 PM Last date & Time for Submission of Bids 12.03.2025 upto 3.00 PM Date & Time of Opening of Technical Bids 13.03.2025 upto 3.00 PM Date & Time of Opening of Finance Bids Will be intimated to technically qualified bidders in due course of time through Central Public Procurement portal. Submission of hard copies of EMD The original EMD in favour of Finance Officer, UoH should be submitted in the University Works Department, University of Hyderabad, Gachibowli, P.O. Central University, HYDERABAD – 500046 up to 3.00 PM on 12. 03 .2025. Sd/- Assistant Engineer( Elect) Sd/- UNIVERSITY ENGINEER Page 3 UNIVERSITY OF HYDERABAD University Works Department Item Rate Tender Contract for Works INDEX S.No Details Page 1 Form-J 4-4 2 Check list for Technical eligibility of Tender. 5-5 3 Bank Details from the Contractors. 6-6 4 General Guidelines. 7-7 5 Method of tender application, tender submission and tender opening. 8-9 6 Eligibility criteria and notice inviting tender. 10-16 7 Proforma of Schedules. 17-22 8 Specialised Agencies. 23-28 9 Schedule of Quantities. 29-30 Signature of the Contractor Page 4 FORM ‘J’ UNDERTAKING I/We undertake and confirm that our firm/partnership firm has not been blacklisted by any state/central departments/PSUs/Autonomous bodies and the last 7 years of its operations. Further that, if such information comes to the notice of the department then I/we shall be debarred for bidding in University of Hyderabad in future forever. Also, if such information comes to the notice of University of Hyderabad on any day before date of start of work, the Engineer-in-charge shall be free to cancel the agreement and to forfeit the entire amount of earnest money Deposit/Performance Guarantee. If further solemnly declare that all the certificates are true to the best of my knowledge. Signature of Bidder(s) or an authorized Officer of the firm with stamp Signature of the Contractor Page 5 Check list for Technical eligibility of Tender Sl No Doc Ref Description of the Document Enclosed Yes/No Remarks 1 NIT Para No 1 Registration of Contractors CPWD/MES/BSNL/Railway/State PWD(B&R) Autonomous bodies or undertakings. 2 NIT Para No 1 Eligible Contractors/ Date of validity of enlistment 3 Details of works completed during last 7 years (Detailed statements to be enclosed) Not less than 40 % of estimated cost (Three works of Electrical completed works) Not less than 50 % of estimated cost (Two works of Electrical completed works) Not less than 80 % of estimated cost (One work of Electrical completed work) (Submit Details of works on which contractor meets specified eligibility criteria) 4 As per the NIT The tenderer shall have to furnish an undertaking in prescribed format. (form J) 5 Annual turnover. 30% of the estimated cost. Signature of the Contractor Page 6 Details of the Contractor S.No. Particulars 1 Name of the Firm 2 Name of the Contractor 3 Contractor Details (a) Mobile (b) E-Mail id 4 Name of the Bank 5 Name of the Branch 6 Account No. (prefix with zeros, if any as given on the cheque book/pass book ) {please attach cancelled cheque} 7 IFSC Code of the Branch 8 MICR Code 9 PAN No. 10 GST No.(if applicable) Signature of the Contractor Page 7 GENERAL GUIDELINES 1. This book of “General Conditions of Contract” is applicable to both types of tenders i.e.” Percentage rate tenders and Item rate tenders”. Accordingly, alternative provisions for conditions Nos. 4, 10 & 12 of the General Rules and Directions are given in this book. The appropriate alternatives will be applicable in specific cases depending on whether this is used for percentage rate tender (CPWD-7) or item rate tender (CPWD-8). 2. CPWD-6, Schedules A to F, special conditions/specifications and drawings only will be issued to intending bidders. The HCU-GCC 2016 form will not be issued along with the Tender Documents but the same shall form part of the agreement to be drawn and signed by both parties after acceptance of tender. The HCU-GCC 2016 can be accessed and downloaded from website www.uohyd.ac.in 3. All blanks are confined to Notice Inviting Tender (CPWD-6) and Schedules A to F. 4. Authority approving the Notice Inviting Tenders (NIT) shall fill up all the blanks in CPWD-6 and in Schedules B to F before issue of Tender Papers. 5. The intending bidders shall quote their rates in Schedule A (Schedule of quantities in CPWD Form 3) 6. The proforma for registers and Schedules A to F are only for information and guidance. These are not to be filled in the Standard Form. The Schedules with all blanks, duly filled, shall be separately issued to all intending tenderers. Signature of the Contractor Page 8 Method of Tender Application, Tender Submission and Tender Opening The intending bidder must read the terms and conditions of CPWD-6 carefully. He should only submit his bid if he considers himself eligible and he is in possession of submission of all the required documents as per NIT. The following Technical and Finance bid documents shall be upload simultaneously with scanned copies in e-procurement web site. The tender documents may also be seen at University of Hyderabad website- www.uohyd.ac.in (A) Technical bid documents 1) The bidders except Micro and Small Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) notified under (MSME) Policy (as per Rule 170 of GFR 2017), should pay EMD @ 2% of Tendered amount (including GST) should be drawn in favor of “Finance Officer, University of Hyderabad” either in form of Bank Guarantee/ fixed deposit receipt of a scheduled bank/demand draft/banker check of a scheduled bank. The original EMD shall be placed in Envelope-1 and closed using suitable adhesive and shall be dropped in the Tender box before the bid opening date and time. The scanned copy of EMD shall be uploaded on the web site. Bids submitted along with EMD in the prescribed form shall be considered for further evaluation of eligibility Criteria. Bids submitted without EMD shall be summarily rejected. The Technical bid shall contain all the documents scanned and uploaded in the concerned web site, based on which the bidder claim to be eligible as per eligibility criteria prescribed in NIT. Any discloser of finance bid in the technical bid documents will lead to summary rejection of bid. 2) Work experience certificates as per Eligibility criteria. 3) Contract registration certificate issued by State or Central Govt., Departments or state/central autonomous bodies undertaking. 4) PAN card & GST Registration Certificate. 5) Latest Income Tax returns for the consecutive three financial years. Immediately preceding the tender date. 6) Turnover Certificate for the consecutive three financial years, immediately preceding the tender date duly certified by the Chartered Accountants. 7) Undertaking as per Form “J”. 8) Other necessary documents as per Tender documents. Page 9 On the due date of opening, the Technical bid of those tenderer who furnished valid EMD will only be opened. On opening of Technical bid, further detailed scrutiny/evaluation will be carried out. During the evaluation of techno commercial bids, the documents furnished by the tenderers will be scrutinized in detail. Any tender, found as not fulfilling the eligibility criteria will be rejected at this stage and such offers will not be considered for further processing. The price bid of only those tenderers who have been qualified during the scrutiny and technical evaluation will be opened separately on a specified date (with due intimation to the qualified bidders) and further processed, as per tender procedure/stipulations. Signature of the Contractor Page 10 Eligibility Criteria and Notice Inviting tender: (1) The bidder shall be a registered/enlisted contractor and should produce definite proof of registration/enlistment under appropriate class issued registered by state or central government departments or state/central autonomous bodies or undertakings. (2) Experience Criteria (Eligibility criteria for participation in tendering). Estimate Cost of the work is Rs. 42,56,700/-(including of GST) (a) Bidders should have satisfactorily completed during last 07 years ending last day of the month prior to the month in which the tenders are invited. (i) One Electrical Substation Works completed 80% of Estimated cost i.e Rs.34,05,360 /- (including of GST) (OR) (ii) Two Electrical Substation works completed each costing not less 50% of Estimated cost i.e. Rs.21,28,350/-including of GST) (OR) (iii) Three Electrical Substation works each costing not less than 40% of Estimated cost i.e Rs. 17,02,680/- (including of GST)Self-Attested copies of experience certificates are to be submitted. (3) Only work completed and certified by competent authority of the organization will be accepted as Experience Certificate. Certificate not issued in the name of bidder (Contractor) or issued by an authority not competent to issue such certificate will not be accepted. Mere work order or purchase order etc issued will not qualify for experience. (3a) The copies of relevant IT returns and Auditor Certified Turnover Certificate for the consecutive three financial years, immediately preceding the tender date. PAN Card, GST Registration certificate should accompany the technical bid. (4) The contractors who were penalized under clause No (2) of General Conditions of Contract during the last one year in UoH campus works will be disqualified and their Technical /Financial bids will not be accepted. (5) Should have had average Annual Financial turnover not less than Rs. 12,77,010 /- i.e., 30% of the estimated cost of the work during the last three years ending 31st March 2024. (6) To become eligible for issue of tender, the tenderer shall have to furnish an undertaking, as perform ‘J’ of the NIT. Signature of the Contractor Page 11 (7) Agreement shall be drawn with the successful tenderer in the prescribed Form No. CPWD 7/8 which is available in the University of Hyderabad website. Tenderer shall quote his rates as per various terms and conditions of the said form which will form part of the agreement. (8) The time allowed for carrying out the work is 1 Months from the start date as defined in clause 5 Scheduled “F” or from the first date of handing over of the site, whichever is later, in accordance with phasing if any indicated in the tender document. The site shall be made available as and when required for execution of work. (9)(a) Tenders shall be accompanied with Earnest money of 2% of estimated cost put to tender/in the receipt of fixed deposit receipt /demand draft/banker check of a scheduled bank issued in favour of Finance Officer, University of Hyderabad payable at Hyderabad. (b) Defect liability period of six (06) months after satisfactory completion of work. (10) The Bidder/contractor, whose tender is accepted, will be required to furnish performance Guarantee of 5% (Five Percent) of the tendered amount within the period specified in Schedule F. This guarantee shall be in the form of cash (in case guarantee amount is less than Rs. 10,000/-) or Deposit at Call receipt of any scheduled bank/Banker’s cheque of any scheduled bank/Demand Draft of any scheduled bank/Pay order of any scheduled bank (in case guarantee amount is more than Rs. 10,000/-) Government Securities or Fixed Deposit Receipts or Guarantee Bonds of any Scheduled Bank in accordance with the prescribed form. In case the contractor fails to deposit the said performance guarantee within the period as indicated in Schedule “F” including the extended period if any, the Earnest Money deposited by the contractor shall be forfeited automatically without any notice to the contractor. (11) The description of the work is as follows: Copies of other drawing and documents pertaining to the works will be open for inspection by the tenderers at the office of above mentioned officer. Tenderers are advised to inspect and examine the building and its area surroundings and satisfy themselves before submitting their tenders. The tenderer shall be responsible for arranging and maintaining at his own cost all materials, tools & plants, water, required for executing the work unless otherwise services provided for in the contract documents. Submission of a specific electricity access, facilities for workers and all other tender by a tenderer implies that he has read this notice and all other contract documents and has made himself aware of the scope and specifications of the work to be done. Signature of the Contractor Page 12 (12) The competent authority on behalf of the University of Hyderabad does not bind himself to accept the lowest or any other tender and reserves to itself the authority to reject any or all the tenders received without the assignment of any reason. All tenders in which any of the prescribed condition is not fulfilled or any condition including that of conditional rebate is put forth by the tenderer shall be summarily rejected. (13) Canvassing whether directly or indirectly, in connection with tenderers is strictly prohibited and the tenders submitted by the contractors who resort to canvassing will be liable to rejection. (14) The University Engineer on behalf of the competent authority of University reserves to himself the right of accepting the whole or any part of the tender and the tenderer shall be bound to perform the same at the rate quoted. (15) No Engineer of Gazette rank or other Gazetted Officer employed in Engineering or Administrative duties in an Engineering Department of the Government of India is allowed to work as a contractor for a period of one year after his retirement from Government service, without the previous permission of the Government of India in writing. This contract is liable to be cancelled if either the contractor or any of his employees is found any time to be such a person who had not obtained the permission of the Government of India as aforesaid before submission of the tender or engagement in the contractor’s service. (16) The tender for the works shall remain open for acceptance for a period of 90 days from the date of opening of tenders/Ninety days from the date of opening of financial bid. If any bidder withdraws his tender before the said period or issue of letter of acceptance, whichever is earlier, or makes any modifications in the terms and conditions of the tender which are not acceptable to the department, then the Government shall, without prejudice to any other right or remedy, be at liberty to forfeit of the said earnest money as aforesaid. Further the tenderer shall not be allowed to participate in the retendering process of the work.
